draft.shortGloss: to wake up; to be awake
draft.emotion: refreshing and calm, acknowledging the start of the day
notes: Intransitive (does not take ने in the past tense). Its transitive counterpart is जगाना (to wake someone up).
In everyday speech, उठना (to get up) is also very commonly used to mean 'to wake up'.

notes: Use जागना (to wake up) for the moment you stop sleeping. If you want to say 'to stay awake' or 'to remain awake', use the form जागते रहना.
Do not confuse this with उठाना, which means 'to wake someone else up' or 'to pick something up'.

faults.quote: Use जागना (to wake up) for the moment you stop sleeping.
faults.why: Contradicts sense 1; जागना itself is commonly used for staying/being awake.
Should mention the transitive counterpart जगाना (to wake someone up) and intransitivity.
